sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:1
items.html: That her light did not return to descend into the vessel that is in her: That is, in the second expansion, in which the coupling emerged only at the level of Hochma, and therefore the lights were interchanged, for the light of Hochma came into the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina into the vessel of Hochma, etc., and the light of Malchut into the vessel of Yesod, and the vessel of Malchut remained without light, as above. (Inner Light, Part 4, Chapter 2, Item 8.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:2
items.html:
In the vessel of Malchut through the posterior of Yesod itself: It has already been explained that all the levels that emerge by way of refinement are regarded as reflected light and judgment; and although there is direct light in them as well, still, since they are drawn through the posterior, that is, by way of the refinement of the coarseness, which is called the anterior, as above, therefore the direct light too is regarded as a phase of judgment.
And this is what he says: “Yesod was illuminating in the vessel of Malchut through the posterior of Yesod,” for all these ten Sefirot, the direct light and the reflected light together, are the phase of posterior and judgment. Indeed, apart from this it must be understood that the whole of the light that descends from Yesod to the vessel of Malchut is entirely reflected light, and there is nothing of direct light in it; for since the place of the coupling and of the screen is in the vessel of Yesod, that is, in phase three, this screen restrains the direct light so that nothing of it expands from phase three downward. Thus everything that descends from Yesod to the vessel of Malchut is only reflected light and not direct light, and this is what the ARI adds and specifies: “in the secret of reflected light,” as said.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:3
items.html: Meets Malchut’s own first light that ascends upward: For this light is at the level of Keter, which regards the greater coarseness as the phase of anterior; whereas the descending reflected light lowers the great coarseness of phase four and prefers phase three, which is more refined than she, and this stands in contradiction to the ascending light of Malchut. Therefore they clash one with the other, as above (Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 9, see there), and it will be further explained in the Inner Observation here.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:4
items.html: And sparks descended from the descending reflected light: And they are called sparks because of the likeness to the sparks that come out from under the hammer, which shine and are extinguished at once, as is written in the Zohar. Indeed, the allegory is not entirely like that which it signifies, for the sparks that come out from under the hammer shine for a moment and are lost immediately, and their place is known no more; whereas these sparks here, and likewise the 288 sparks, although they were extinguished at once because of the departure of the coupling to a higher phase, which is phase two, nevertheless they were not lost from there, for there is no absence in spirituality, as is known, and their self and their substance remained there, and afterwards they returned to their former strength when the second expansion arrived there, as is written in its place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:5
items.html: Into the vessel of Malchut: It is the coarse light that remains below after the departure of the first expansion, which is the very self of the vessels belonging to the first expansion of Akudim, where the lights left their records, and where the sparks fell from the descending reflected light, as the ARI wrote above (Part 4, Chapter 2, Item 10, see there and in the Inner Light).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:6
items.html: And from them the phase of the vessel of Yesod was made: That is, for the second expansion that comes afterwards, which is called the Partzuf AB of AK; but the vessel of Yesod of Akudim that is here was made from the coarse light that remains below after the departure of the first expansion, as above (see above item).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:7
items.html: And this is the secret of the Tagin: Look well above at the words of the ARI, Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 9, and in the Inner Light, Item 80, where this is explained at length. And know that after the coupling ceased in the upper vessel and it ascended above it — whereupon the illumination of the coupling necessarily ceased from the lower vessel as well — then the sparks that had descended there are also found to be extinguished. Therefore the record, which was above the vessel, is able once again to return and clothe in the vessel as at first (see above in the Inner Light, Chapter 3, Item 80). And nevertheless that illumination from afar, which is called Tagin, did not cease from the vessel even after this, because there is no absence in spirituality, as is known, in the secret of “the Shechina has never moved,” etc.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:8
items.html: Except for Keter, which left the record for the need of Hochma: Meaning that that record became the phase of the vessel of the male of the light of Hochma, in the Keter of the second expansion, which is called AB of AK. And this is what the ARI writes: “except for Keter, which left the record for the need of Hochma but did not make the phase of a vessel.” That is, that it did not make the phase of a vessel for the need of the female of the light of Hochma in the vessel of Keter of the second expansion, as is written just below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:9
items.html:
But did not make the phase of a vessel: The ARI has already written above (Chapter 2, Item 10) that the very phase of the vessels of Akudim was made from the coarse light that remains from the light of the departure itself, see there. And from this you will understand that what is spoken of here is not the vessel of Keter itself, but rather the intention is upon the vessels of the second expansion, which comes after the present departure, where in the vessel of Keter there is a phase of male and a phase of female. And so too in the vessels of Hochma and Bina and Yesod and Malchut, as the ARI writes below (Item 6, and in Etz Chaim, in the Gate of Matey ve Lo Matey, Chapter 3).
Now the vessels of the males there were made from the records that remained in the vessels of Akudim; and the vessels of the females were made from the sparks that fall from the descending reflected light into the vessels of Akudim that are here, as is written there in the words of the ARI.
And this is what he says: “except for Keter, which left the record for the need of Hochma,” that is, the vessel of the male of the light of Hochma that is in the vessel of Keter of the second expansion. “But did not make the phase of a vessel” — meaning, for the need of the female that is there, as is written in the adjacent item below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:10
items.html: Striking against what is above them: Meaning, by means of a coupling by striking in the phase that is above the vessel that was emptied of the light, reflected light is drawn and descends to the vessel that was emptied. That is, after the light departed from the vessel of Malchut — which is because the screen of phase four was refined to phase three, which is Yesod — and the coupling was made in the vessel of Yesod, then reflected light descends from the illumination of this coupling to Malchut, who was emptied of the light. And this is what he says: “by means of striking against what is above them” — the reflected light is drawn to the vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:11
items.html: And the striking of the record: The record that remained in the vessel that was emptied strikes at the reflected light that descends to its vessel, because it is the opposite of the descending reflected light, as said above. And by means of this striking, sparks were born and separated from the descending reflected light and fall into the vessel that was emptied, and from these sparks the vessels were made.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:12
items.html: The phase of the vessels was made: That is, the vessels for the need of the vessels of the second expansion; but the vessels of Akudim of the first expansion were made from the coarse light, as above in the words of the ARI, Chapter 2, Item 10 (and see the Inner Light, Chapter 2, Item 100).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:13
items.html: For Keter there is none who strikes at its record in its ascent: For when the screen arrives at complete refinement, like the phase of the Emanator, then its force has already ceased, and there is no longer any coupling by striking in it that would bring reflected light down into the vessel of Keter after it was emptied of the light. “Therefore its vessel was not yet completed,” for there are no sparks there from the descending reflected light, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:14
items.html:
Indeed, after these Sefirot received from the Emanator they returned to their place: And one must understand very well this matter of the reception that the Sefirot received from the Emanator after their ascent to Him, of which the ARI speaks here. And you will understand the matter after you know thoroughly the matter of the departure of the ten Sefirot of the Guf [body] and their ascent to the Emanator. And know that all of this is drawn from and bound up with the light of Malchut alone, whose meaning is the screen and the reflected light that are in Malchut; for there is no other light in Malchut, since she never receives any direct light, as is known. Therefore the whole of the light in her is only the reflected light, which is drawn by means of a coupling by striking upon the screen that is in her. Thus the coarseness of phase four is the vessel of Malchut, and the screen that restrains the upper light from expanding into the coarseness of phase four, together with the reflected light that ascends on its account, are reckoned as the light of Malchut.
And from this you will understand that the principal matter of the ascent of the lights to the Emanator is bound up with the ascent of Malchut alone. For “ascends” means that it is refined and equalizes its form with the upper one, since equivalence of form with the upper one brings it to the upper one and joins it there, as is known. Now the matter of the refinement of the coarseness applies only in Malchut, in whom there is coarseness; whereas in the first nine Sefirot, in which there is as yet no phase of a vessel at all, and which are reckoned here as pure light only (as above in the words of the ARI, Part 4, Chapter 1, Item 11), how could the matter of the refinement of the coarseness be said of them? Rather it is certain that the matter of the ascent and the refinement is said of Malchut alone. And the intention is not upon the vessel of Malchut, for the vessels are never refined of their coarseness (as is written in Part 2, answer 43), but rather the intention is upon the screen that is set in the vessel of Malchut (as is written above in the Inner Light, Chapter 2, Item 10, see there).
And you already know the matter of the four levels that emerge by means of a coupling by striking upon the screen, from the beginning of its refinement until it is refined to the phase of the Emanator. And know that these levels, which go on diminishing, are themselves the Sefirot of which the ARI says here that they ascended to the Emanator. And although there are ten Sefirot in each and every level, nevertheless they are named only after the uppermost Sefira of their level: for the level of phase three, although it contains ten Sefirot up to the level of Hochma, is called in its entirety only by the name of the light of Hochma alone, that is, after the uppermost Sefira of the level. And likewise the ten Sefirot of the level from phase two, which reaches up to Bina, is called Bina alone; and that of phase one by the name ZA; and that of the phase of Keter and root by the name Malchut.
Know also that all these records, which the lights of Akudim left in their vessels after their departure, all of them remained only in the vessel of Malchut, since she is the single vessel for all the ten Sefirot of Akudim (as above). And this is the coarse light that the ARI brings above (Chapter 2, Item 10), which is the phase of the vessels of Akudim themselves, where the lights left their records. It is therefore necessarily the phase of Malchut alone, since in the first nine there is no coarseness at all, as above. And it was explained in the Inner Light there that this coarse light is the secret of the reflected light in Malchut, which expanded with it from herself and within herself, to clothe the ten Sefirot of direct light from above downward, which is called Guf (see there). Thus it is explained that all the records that remained from the first expansion after its departure necessarily remained in Malchut alone.
And it was explained that Malchut is included of all the records that remained from the first expansion. Therefore, after the screen ascended to the Malchut of the Rosh [head] — whose meaning is that the screen was refined of all its coarseness and came into equivalence of form with the Malchut of the Rosh — it is regarded that the screen that ascended is likewise included of all the records that remained in Malchut, except for the record of phase four, because the last phase leaves no record (as in the words of the ARI in Part 4, Chapter 3, Item 1, see there in the Inner Light). Now you will understand the words of the ARI here, who says: “after these Sefirot received from the Emanator they returned to their place, except for Keter.”
That is, after the screen of the Malchut of the Guf ascended to the Malchut of the Rosh — which is called the phase of Emanator with respect to the Guf, as is known — and this by force of the equivalence of form with it, as above, it follows from this that it joined and was included with the screen that is in the Malchut of the Rosh as though they were one phase. And since the screen in the Malchut of the Rosh is found there in a perpetual coupling by striking, for there is no refinement in the Rosh, as is known, therefore the screen of the Guf too, which ascended and was included with it, is found to serve together with it for the coupling by striking and for the raising of reflected light from below upward that operates in the Rosh, for it was included in that same phase of coarseness that is in the screen in the Malchut of the Rosh.
And you already know that these records, which remained in the Malchut of the Guf, are included in the screen that ascended to the Rosh, and that they reach only up to the coarseness of phase three, for from the coarseness of phase four no record remained, as above. Therefore, after the screen of the Guf was included in and came into the phase of the coupling of the screen of the Rosh, and received from it the coarseness of from below upward that is included in it, then those records included in it from the Malchut of the Guf were awakened once more and returned to their coarseness as at first, that is, to the coarseness of from above downward as operates in the Guf. Thus, at first the screen was included in the Malchut of the Rosh and became coarse with the coarseness of from below upward that operates in the Rosh; and afterwards the records included in the screen were awakened and became coarse as well, and in them the coarseness was reversed and became the phase of from above downward.
And you must know the great difference between the coarseness of from below upward and the coarseness of from above downward. For from below upward means, as it were, a phase of resistance to clothing, and in any case there is no relation of clothing there at all; therefore it is the phase of Rosh, which is called Keter or Ein Sof [infinity]. Its opposite is the phase of coarseness of from above downward, whose meaning is a phase of complete clothing of the direct light; therefore it is called Guf or emanated being, and it is never called by the name Ein Sof or Emanator. And this discernment operates in the Rosh and Guf of all the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] in the worlds.
Therefore, at the time when the screen was refined of all its coarseness entirely, so that it equalized its form with the phase of the Malchut of the Rosh, which is entirely clean of the phase of coarseness of from above downward, as above, it is understood of itself that the records included in it were entirely quiescent, and are reckoned as though they were not in existence at all. And then the screen of the Guf was included in the screen of the Rosh, in the coarseness of from below upward. Indeed, since the screen became coarse — although it is only the coarseness of from below upward — nevertheless those quiescent and resting records included in the screen were awakened because of this and rose to life, that is, they too became coarse. Yet since these records came from the Guf, where they had already been in a relation of clothing, it follows of itself that this coarseness was reversed in them into the phase of from above downward, into the phase of Guf. And through this the screen acquired a disparity of form very far from the Rosh, that is, by the measure of the difference from the phase of Rosh to the phase of Guf.
And it follows that at that very moment when the coarseness of from above downward was revealed in the screen, which is the phase of Guf, it is regarded that the screen once again went out from the Rosh and descended to the Guf — yet not to phase four of the Guf, which is called Tabur, but only to phase three of the Guf, which is called Chazeh [chest]. And this is because the screen was able to become coarse only up to phase three, since phase four left no record in the screen, as above.
And you find that the screen that ascended to the Emanator attained there two phases of coarseness: namely, the coarseness of from below upward, by force of its having first been included in the Malchut of the Rosh; and the coarseness of from above downward, which was awakened and returned to the records included in it. Therefore, when the screen went out from the Malchut of the Rosh to the place of the Chazeh in the Guf, as above, it first brought forth the phase of a coupling by striking of the phase of ten Sefirot of Rosh, from the Chazeh upward, by force of the coarseness of from below upward included in it — and that only at the level of Hochma, since there is in it only the coarseness of phase three. And afterwards it expanded from the Chazeh downward into the phase of ten Sefirot of Guf, by force of the coarseness of from above downward included in it. And this is what is called the second expansion.
And this is what he says: “after these Sefirot received from the Emanator.” That is, after the screen of the Guf was entirely refined, which is termed that it ascended to the Emanator, who is the Malchut of the Rosh, as above, it received there once again the force to return and expand into the clothing of ten Sefirot as at first; that is, that the coarseness in the records within it was awakened once more, up to phase three. Then it returned to its place, to the Malchut of the Guf, as at first, as above, and then the second expansion emerged upon it in ten Sefirot of Rosh and Guf as at first, as above. And this is what he says: “they returned to their place,” namely to the place of the Malchut of the Guf, as has been explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:15
items.html: Except for Keter: And this is because the screen did not become coarse further in its inclusion in the Malchut of the Rosh [head], but only up to phase three, for phase four left no record (see above item); and the expansion that emerges upon a screen of phase three reaches only to the level of Hochma, and the light of Keter is lacking. And this is what he says: “they all returned to their place, except for Keter.” It follows that the light of Hochma clothes in the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, and the light of ZA in the vessel of Bina, and the light of Malchut in the vessel of ZA, and Malchut remained without light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:16
items.html: The vessel of Keter was made only upon the return: That is, the vessel of the Nukva of Keter, which is the light of Hochma that clothes in the vessel of Keter, which is lacking here for the reason explained above (this chapter, Item 4, and see the Inner Light there).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:17
items.html: The light of Hochma struck at the record that Keter left in it in its place: The light of the level of Hochma that comes to clothe in the vessel of Keter is similar in nature to the descending reflected light (mentioned above in the words of the ARI, in Chapter 3, Item 9, and in the Inner Light there), which stands in contradiction to the light of the record, and they strike one against the other.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:18
items.html: And these strikings were double: For the record that remains from the first expansion, since it is higher than Hochma — for its level reaches up to Keter — therefore it stands in contradiction to the light of Hochma that comes now, whose level reaches only up to Hochma (as in the Inner Light above, Chapter 3, Item 60, see there). And likewise there is an advantage to the light of Hochma in that it now comes from above downward in order to clothe in the vessels, which is not so with the record, in which is embedded the desire to depart from the phase of clothing, although it does not actually ascend (as above in the words of the ARI, Chapter 3, Item 9, and in the Inner Light there, Item 70, see there).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:19
items.html: One for the record of Keter and one for the Hochma that came now: Meaning that the coarse light that fell from the record because of the striking of the light of Hochma upon it became a vessel for the light of the record, which is the phase of the male of the vessel of Keter. And from the sparks that fell from the light of Hochma because of the striking of the light of the record upon it, the vessel was made for the light of Hochma that is in the vessel of Keter, which is the phase of the female of the vessel of Keter. And although there is already a vessel for the male of the vessel of Keter, as above, nevertheless by means of the striking of the light of Hochma it is completed and renewed (as is written at length in Part 5).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:20
items.html: Expounded at length on this elsewhere: This is in Etz Chaim, the Gate of Matey ve Lo Matey, Chapter 3.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:21
items.html: The concealment of the lights of Akudim and their ascent into their Emanator: For both of these came about through the ascent of the lights to the Emanator, whose meaning is the refinement of the screen. Therefore the ways too are alike one to the other, as is written at length in my book Panim Meirot uMasbirot on the Etz Chaim, in the matters of the breaking of the vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:4:22
items.html: The corruption was in order to correct, and the demolishing in order to build: For by means of the refinement in the screen the levels went on diminishing, and from every upper phase sparks fell to the phase below it, which is the beginning of the association of the quality of mercy with judgment, for the sparks of an upper phase are reckoned as the quality of mercy with respect to the lower one. And it is known that the association of the quality of mercy with judgment is the foundation for the existence of the world, as above (Inner Light, Chapter 1, Item 4, Sub Header, “And this”). And this is what he says: “here in Akudim the corruption was in order to correct, and the demolishing in order to build,” for this is similar to the breaking of the vessels, where the sparks fell in order to revive them through the quality of mercy. And the whole difference between them is that here there was only corruption, while there “there was an actual nullification and death” (as is written at length in my commentaries Panim Meirot and Panim Masbirot on the matter of the breaking of the vessels).
